translation.text: And now[a], my son Methuselah, I will show you all my visions that I have seen before you; I will recount them.

footnotes.text: The wording uses two verbs of disclosure: first 'show,' then 'recount/tell.' The pairing emphasizes both visionary display and spoken narration.

source.text: ክልኤተ፡ ራእየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ እንበለ፡ እንሣእ፡ ብእሲተ፡ ወአሐዱሂ፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ኢይትማሰል፡ ምስለ፡ ካልኡ፡ ቀዳማየ፡ አመ፡ እትሜሀር፡ መጽሐፈ፡ ወ*ካልአ፡ እንበለ፡ እንሥእ፡ ለእምከ፡ ርኢኩ፡ ራእየ፡ ጽኑዐ፡ ወበእንቲአሆሙ፡ አስተብቋዕክዎ፡ ለእግዚእ።

translation.text: I saw two visions before I took a wife[a], and one of them was not like the other: the first when I was learning the book, and the second before I took your mother—I saw a mighty vision[d][c][b]; and concerning them I made supplication to the Lord.

footnotes.text: Or 'when I was being taught the book.' The Ge'ez verb may imply either learning or being instructed.
'A mighty vision' may also be rendered 'a severe' or 'powerful vision,' emphasizing the intensity of the revelation.
The phrase 'concerning them' could also mean 'because of them,' indicating that the visions prompted Enoch's prayer.
Or 'and the second, before I took your mother, I saw a mighty vision'.

source.text: ስኩበ፡ ኮንኩ፡ በቤት፡ መላሕእል፡ እምሑውየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ በራእይ፡ ሰማይ፡ ይትነጻጻ፡ ወይትሀየድ፡ ወይወድቅ፡ *ዲበ፡ ምድር።

translation.text: I was lying down in the house of my grandfather Mahalalel[a], and I saw in a vision that the heaven was being cleansed and swept away[c][b], and it fell upon the earth.

footnotes.text: Or 'the sky was being cleansed and swept away.' The Ge'ez wording is vivid but somewhat uncertain in the middle verb, which likely conveys violent removal before the fall to earth.
Or 'was being cleansed and swept away'.
Or 'I lay down'.

source.text: ወሶበ፡ ይወድቅ፡ ዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ርኢክዋ፡ ለምድር፡ ከመ፡ ትትወሐጥ፡ ውስተ፡ ቀላይ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ወአድባር፡ ዲበ፡ አድባር፡ ይስቀሉ፡ ወአውግር፡ *ዲበ፡ አውግር፡ ይሰጠሙ፡ ወዕፀወ፡ ነዋኃት፡ ይትገዘሙ፡ እምጕንዶቲሆሙ፡ ወ*ይትገደፉ፡ *ወይሰጠሙ፡ ውስተ፡ ቀላይ።

translation.text: And when it fell upon the earth[a], I saw the earth being swallowed into a great abyss, and mountains were suspended upon mountains, and hills sank down upon hills[d][c][b], and tall trees were cut off from their trunks and were thrown down and sank into the abyss.

footnotes.text: Or 'a great deep' or 'a great chasm.' The Ge'ez term denotes a vast depth; 'abyss' best preserves the apocalyptic force.
The phrase 'mountains were suspended upon mountains' is intentionally retained as a strange visionary image rather than smoothed into a more ordinary description.
The wording about the trees may also be understood more generally as being severed from their base or stock.
Or 'were torn up from their trunks'.

source.text: ወ*እምኔሁ፡ ወድቀ፡ ነገር፡ ውስተ፡ አፉየ፡ ወ*አንሣእኩ፡ እጽራሕ፡ ወእቤ፡ ተሐጕለት፡ ምድር።

translation.text: And a word fell into my mouth because of it[a], and I lifted up a cry and said[d][c][b], “The earth is destroyed.”

footnotes.text: Or 'from it' or 'thereupon'; the opening phrase may mark source, cause, or sequence from the preceding vision.
Literally, 'a word fell into my mouth,' an idiom for an utterance that came upon the speaker.
The verb behind 'is swallowed up' may also be understood more generally as 'is overwhelmed' or 'has perished.'
Or 'The earth is swallowed up.'.

source.text: ወመላእያል፡ እምሔውየ፡ አንሥአኒ፡ እንዘ፡ እነ፡ እስክብ፡ ኀቤሁ፡ ወይቤለኒ፡ ምንት፡ ከመዝ፡ ትጸርኅ፡ ወልድየ፡ ወ*ለምንት፡ ከመዝ፡ ትአወዩ።

translation.text: And Malyal my grandfather lifted me up while I was lying beside him[a], and he said to me, “Why do you cry out like this, my son[c][b], and why do you lament like this?”

footnotes.text: The name rendered 'Malyal' likely reflects the patriarch Mahalalel in Ethiopic form; some translators normalize the name.
The wording distinguishes two related actions: first a loud crying out, then lamenting or grieving.
Or 'And Malyal lifted me up from where I was'.

source.text: ወ*ነገርክዎ፡ *ኵሎ፡ ራእየ፡ ዘርኢኩ፡ ወይቤለኒ፡ ከመ፡ ጽኑዐ፡ ርኢከ፡ ወልድየ፡ ወኃያለ፡ ርእየ፡ ሕልምከ፡ *ኅቡኣተ፡ ኵሉ፡ ኃጢአተ፡ ምድር፡ ወትሰጠም፡ ሀለወት፡ ውስተ፡ ቀላይት፡ ወ*ተሐጕል፡ ኅጕለ፡ ዐቢየ።

translation.text: And I told him all the vision that I had seen[a], and he said to me, “Severe is the sight you have seen, my son, and mighty is the vision of your dream: it reveals all the hidden sin of the earth[f][e][d][c][b], and it is about to sink into the abyss and be destroyed with a great destruction.”

footnotes.text: The clause 'it has hidden all the sin of the earth' is difficult. The Ethiopic appears to use a verb meaning 'hide' or 'conceal'; some interpreters understand the line more broadly as the dream exposing or encompassing the earth's sin and its judgment.
'Abyss' renders a term that can also denote the deep or sea; the apocalyptic context favors the more cosmic sense.
The final expression is textually and lexically difficult; the sense is that of being enclosed or covered over in overwhelming darkness or gloom.
Or 'it has hidden all the sin of the earth'.
Or 'and it will sink while it is in the abyss'.
Or 'and it will be wrapped in great darkness'.

source.text: ወይእዜኒ፡ ወልድየ፡ ተንሥእ፡ ወአስተብቍዖ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ ስብሐት፡ እስመ፡ መሃይምን፡ አንተ፡ ከመ፡ ይትረፍ፡ ትራፍ፡ ዲበ፡ ምድር፡ *ወኢይደምስሳ፡ ለኵላ፡ ምድር።

translation.text: And now[a], my son, rise and make your petition to the Lord of glory, since you are faithful[b], that a remnant may remain upon the earth and that he may not wipe out the whole earth.

footnotes.text: The Ge'ez uses a doubled expression for what is left over ('remain a remnant' / 'be left as residue'), which is rendered here as 'a remnant may remain' to preserve the emphasis.
The title 'Lord of glory' is kept as a formal divine epithet rather than simplified to 'glorious Lord.'

source.text: ወልድየ፡ እምሰማይ፡ ይሄሉ፡ ኵሉዝ፡ ዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ወዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ይከውን፡ ሐጕል፡ ዐቢይ።

translation.text: My son[a], from heaven all this will come upon the earth[c][b], and upon the earth there will be a great destruction.

footnotes.text: The phrase rendered 'all this' may also be understood more generally as 'all' or 'all these things'; the Ge'ez form is somewhat difficult in this OCR witness.
'Earth' could in some contexts be rendered 'land,' but the broader apocalyptic setting favors the cosmic sense.
Or 'And my son from heaven will say, ‘Let all this be upon the earth, and upon the earth there shall be a great destruction.’'.

source.text: ወእምኔሁ፡ ተንሣእኩ፡ ወጸለይኩ፡ ወአስተብቋዕኩ፡ ወሰአልኩ፡ ወ*ጸሎትየ፡ ጸሐፍኩ፡ ለትውልደ፡ ዓለም፡ ወኵሎ፡ አርአየከ፡ ወልድየ፡ ማቱሳላ።

translation.text: And after this I arose and prayed and entreated and asked[a], and I wrote down my prayer for the generations of the world; and I showed you everything[b], my son Methuselah.

footnotes.text: Or 'for all future generations' or 'for the generations forever'; the Ge'ez phrase can carry the sense of enduring generations beyond the present age.
Or 'and I showed everything to you'.

source.text: ወ*ሶበ፡ ወፃእኩ፡ ታሕተ፡ ወርኢክዎ፡ ለሰማይ፡ ወ*ለፀሐይ፡ ይወጽእ፡ እምሥራቅ፡ ወወርኅ፡ ይወርድ፡ እምዕራብ፡ ወ*ውሑዳት፡ ከዋክብት፡ ወኵሉ፡ *ምድር፡ ወኵሉ፡ †ዘአመረ፡ *ዲበ፡ ቀዳሚ፡ ወባረክዎ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ ኵኔ፡ ወሎቱ፡ ወሀብኩ፡ ዕበየ፡ እስመ፡ *አውፅአ፡ ፀሐየ፡ እመኅከወ፡ ምሥራቅ፡ ወዐርገ፡ ወሠረቀ፡ ዲበ፡ ገጸ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወአንሥአ፡ ወየሐውር፡ ፍኖተ፡ እንተ፡ ተርእየት፡ ሎቱ።

translation.text: And when I went out below[a] and saw the heaven, and the sun rising in the east, and the moon setting in the west, and a few stars, and the whole earth, and everything as He had known it in the beginning[b], then I blessed the Lord of judgment and extolled Him, because He had brought forth the sun from the windows of the east, and it ascended and rose on the face of the heaven, and set out and followed the path which He showed it.[c]

footnotes.text: The selected source has a spatial term rendered below/down; its exact setting is not identified geographically.

Charles1906printed161note12discusses this dagger-marked corrupt clause, comparing knew/saw with proposed made/built readings. The current POB known wording is retained provisionally, not certified or silently harmonized with a creation account.

The selected ending describes a path shown to the sun in a passive construction. Current POB makes the contextual agent explicit with He; this is an English interpretation, not a separately expressed divine name in that clause.
